l.i: Utque leues stipulæ crepitanti vruntur ab igni,
Tui furoris æstus hostem perdidit.
Nam simul atque tuis de naribus halitus ingens
Afflauit æquor, protinus stantes aquæ
Densari in cumulum, & medio concrescere
ponto, Tuæque genti militauerunt freta.
Dixerat ille ferox, Iam persequar, assequar istos,
Et spolia compos mox opima diuidam.
Nunc totam expleta satiabo libidine mentem,
Striƈtoque[?] ferro hæc sternet euersos manus:
Quid dignum hæc tanto gessit fiducia fastu? Te slante tantum,
protinus tunctum[?] mare Innuasit tumidos, & plumbi more profundo
Rapide voluta mersit unda gurgite.
Ergo cunctorum Deus o supreme Deorum,
Quis comparabit se tibi, quis confere-
t? Tu magnus, tu terribilis, tu laude tuorum
Gestorum in omne dignus suum suspici[?].
Qui pius extensa media inter prælia dextra,
Tellure ab ima denoratis hostibus,
Exemptum hunc morti populum deducis, &
ipse In sede tuta fortis illum collocas.
Audiet hic circum externi gens incola cæli,
Simulque gelidus occupabit hanc tremor.
Culta Palestina sindunt qui ingera[?] terræ
Toti expauescent, nec minus perterritos
Palmiferam proceres quicunque tuentur Idumen
Inuadet horror, & Moabi principes,

main_text.l: [The page ends with the catchword "Atque" at the lower right; it is not repeated in the text.]

page.notes: Verse has no clear stanza indents on this scan, so the whole passage is one paragraph. Doubtful readings: "Striƈtoque" (ligature of ct, read as Strictoque), "tunctum" (uncertain), "ingera" (uncertain), "suspici" (ends the line, possibly suspici). "Innuasit" read as printed; may be a misprint for Innuasit. Printed spelling kept throughout.
